conventions.convention: Quantum integers satisfy [0]=0, [1]=1 and [r+1]=δ[r]−[r−1]. The recurrence quantum characteristic is the least positive vanishing index, or infinity. For complex δ=q+q⁻¹, this differs from ord(q²) at q=±1: the latter is 1 and the former is infinity.
The Gram formula uses arc count p and defect count t=n−2p. Its entire rational product represents a polynomial in δ; individual quotients need not specialize separately.
The normalized closure trace is defined over C only for δ≠0, with τ_n(D)=δ^(c(D)−n) and τ_n(1)=1.
The complex recursion starts with p₀=p₁=1 and requires [2],…,[n] nonzero to construct p_n. Failure of this recursion is not asserted to imply nonexistence of an annihilating idempotent.
Quantum binomials are integer polynomial values B_{n,k}(δ), including k=0,n; specialized values are never defined by dividing vanishing factorials.
Normalization means identity-diagram coefficient ε(e)=1. The field criterion includes zero loop value, characteristic two and ranks zero and one; it does not assert arbitrary-ring descent.
For positive characteristic p and finite quantum characteristic ℓ, p(i)=ℓp^(i−1) for i≥1. The characteristic-zero finite-ℓ branch instead permits n=aℓ−1 for every positive integer a.

load_bearing.statement: For q∈C×, δ=q+q⁻¹, n≥0 and 0≤p≤⌊n/2⌋, det G_{n,p}=∏_{j=1}^p([n−2p+1+j]_q/[j]_q)^{d_{n,p−j}}, where d_{n,r}=binom(n,r)−binom(n,r−1). The entire product is interpreted as its polynomial in δ.
Over a field K, a normalized idempotent e∈TL_n(K,δ) with d_i e=0 for 1≤i<n exists if and only if every B_{n,k}(δ), 0≤k≤n, is nonzero. Every such e also satisfies ed_i=0 and is unique.

For A=Z[q,q⁻¹] and δ=q+q⁻¹, the stated cup and cap maps define ρ_n:TL_n(R,δ)→End_R(V_n) for every commutative A-algebra R. Over A this map has an A-linear left inverse that survives every base change, and hence is injective over every such R.
The entire row B_{n,k}(δ), 0≤k≤n, is nonzero exactly at every finite n if ℓ=∞; at n<ℓ or n=aℓp^(i−1)−1 with i≥1 and 1≤a
For every n≥0, the complex algebra TL_n(C,δ) is semisimple if and only if every link-state cell form φ_{n,t} is nondegenerate.
For δ∈C× and [2],…,[n] nonzero, p_n is a nonzero idempotent annihilated on both sides by all d_i, its corner is Cp_n, and τ_n(p_n)=[n+1]/δ^n.

concerns.concern: F5 says, “Every diagram generator spans the diagram algebra together with the unit”. The cited supplier proves that generator words span, not that individual generators and the unit linearly span the algebra. Step 5.1 uses the correct generator-word statement, so this is a wording correction to F5 rather than a gap in the argument.

alerts.finding: In lem-temperley-lieb-critical-standard-modules-are-simple, Step 3.1 says, “Steps 1.1–2.2 therefore give” determinant nonvanishing. There is no Step 2.2: the relevant preceding steps are 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1. The trailing tags already cite existing steps, and the determinant argument itself closes.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and link-state definition, action, dimension, invariant form, restriction filtration, cellular basis and simple-quotient items against their uses. The owned proofs retain right-module orientation, t=n−2p, the exact restriction submodule/quotient and the distinction between a zero cell-form quotient and an actual module head.

Checked downstream uses of the quantum integers, Gram identity, polynomial quantum binomials, split integral representation and field projector criterion. Critical-label factors have removable limits; the arbitrary-field Gram extension is separately justified by clearing integer polynomial denominators. Ring descent is separately proved rather than attributed to the field theorem. The page preserves the complex-order/recurrence-characteristic distinction and the trace-radical/Jacobson-radical distinction.
